source.name: sp_ProcessOrder

assumptions: PostgreSQL procedures are called within an existing transaction or auto-commit mode; explicit BEGIN/COMMIT removed as procedures don't control transactions in the same way
SCOPE_IDENTITY() converted to RETURNING clause which is the PostgreSQL idiomatic approach
INT type mapping is direct (INT to INT)
DECIMAL(10,2) maps directly to PostgreSQL DECIMAL(10,2)
Schema 'dbo' exists in PostgreSQL or will be created separately
Tables Products, Orders, and OrderItems exist with matching column names and types
OUTPUT parameter converted to INOUT parameter in PostgreSQL
Custom error code 50001 mapped to PostgreSQL ERRCODE 'P0001' (raise_exception)
Added NULL check for product lookup as SELECT INTO will set variable to NULL if no row found

reviewFlags.reason: PostgreSQL procedures handle transactions differently than SQL Server. In PostgreSQL 11+, procedures can control transactions with COMMIT/ROLLBACK, but the converted code relies on automatic transaction management. If explicit transaction control is needed, consider using a function or adjusting the calling context.

SQL Server THROW with error number 50001 converted to RAISE EXCEPTION with ERRCODE 'P0001'. Verify that calling applications can handle PostgreSQL error codes appropriately. The error state parameter (1) is not directly supported in PostgreSQL.
Converted to use RETURNING clause which is more idiomatic in PostgreSQL. Verify that the OrderID column has a default value (SERIAL, IDENTITY, or sequence) to generate the ID automatically.
Added explicit NULL check after SELECT INTO. In PostgreSQL, if no row is found, the variable is set to NULL rather than raising an error. Verify this behavior matches business requirements.

compatibilityNotes.description: PostgreSQL procedures in versions 11+ support transaction control with COMMIT/ROLLBACK, but the behavior differs from SQL Server. The converted procedure relies on the calling context's transaction. If called outside a transaction block, each statement auto-commits.
SQL Server OUTPUT parameters map to PostgreSQL INOUT parameters. The calling syntax differs: SQL Server uses EXEC with OUTPUT keyword, PostgreSQL uses CALL with a variable that gets updated.

SQL Server custom error numbers (50001) don't have direct equivalents in PostgreSQL. Mapped to SQLSTATE 'P0001' (raise_exception). Applications may need to parse error messages or use custom error tables for error code mapping.
SCOPE_IDENTITY() converted to RETURNING clause. This is functionally equivalent but syntactically different. Ensure OrderID column is defined as SERIAL, IDENTITY, or has a DEFAULT nextval() sequence.
PostgreSQL doesn't have an equivalent to SET NOCOUNT ON. Row count behavior is inherently different between the two systems and typically doesn't affect procedure logic.
